breakpoints.note: The PoC file is at least 50 bytes (the fuzzer minimum). fgets successfully reads data into thisline and returns non-NULL, entering the while-loop body. The line-too-long realloc branch at line 1884 is not taken because end - line (0) != linesize - 1 (2047). Execution falls through directly to the vulnerable *(end - 1) = 0 at line 1909.

breakpoints.code: while (fgets(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, f) != NULL)
breakpoints.note: fgets reads attacker-controlled data from the PoC file into the heap-allocated buffer thisline. The PoC data begins with a NUL byte (0x00), so the buffer's first byte is '\0'.

The code unconditionally dereferences *(end - 1) without first checking that end > line. When end == line (because the string is empty due to a leading NUL byte), end - 1 points before the heap buffer. The fix adds the guard end > line before the dereference.

Writes a NUL byte at end - 1. With end == line == thisline, this writes to thisline - 1, which is 1 byte before the start of the 2048-byte heap allocation. ASan detects heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1 at 1 byte to the left of the allocated region.
